GERMANY FACES NEW JOB CUTS AS ECONOMIC RECOVERY FALTERS Nearly one-third of German companies plan to cut jobs in 2027, according to a survey of more than 1,000 firms by the German Economic Institute (IW). 32% expect layoffs, up from 29% in spring, while only one in six plans to hire. Nearly 40% intend to reduce investment, and 80% expect production to stagnate or decline. US 10-YEAR TREASURY AUCTION SEES WEAKER DEMAND AS YIELD TOPS 5% The US Treasury sold $42 billion in 10-year notes at a high yield of 5.02%, above the 5.010% when-issued yield before the auction. The bid-to-cover ratio fell to 2.46 from 2.77 at the previous auction, signaling weaker investor demand. The auction tailed by 1 basis point, as investors demanded a higher yield to absorb the debt. Treasury yields are back above 5%, adding pressure to bonds, borrowing costs and equity valuations.

MARSH PUSHES FED TO EASE BANK CAPITAL RULES FOR AI LOANS Marsh ($MRSH) is lobbying US regulators to reduce capital requirements on bank loans protected by credit risk insurance, as AI data-center lending surges. Barclays is seeking insurance on over $10B in data-center debt, while HSBC is exploring similar deals. With global data-center spending projected to reach $6.7T by 2030, lenders are seeking ways to offload AI credit risk. A Fed decision could come by year-end.

NVDA - INVESTORS RUSH TO BUY NVIDIA DIP DESPITE CEO CRISIS Nearly 90% of Nvidia trades by Saxo clients from Monday to Wednesday were buys, signaling aggressive dip-buying. Nvidia was traded 12 times more than any other stock on the platform. Yet shares fell another 8.4% premarket Thursday as the board weighed Jensen Huang's future. Saxo warns investors may be underestimating succession risk, with no obvious replacement for Huang.
